An SC bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi made the remarks while hearing a plea concerning the proposed gathering by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) at Central Park in Connaught Place. The court said it hoped protesters, traders and authorities would find a way to accommodate their competing interests. The court also warned that it could award compensation if restrictions linked to the protests disproportionately affected businesses and livelihoods. What did the top court say? “We hope better sense will prevail on everyone. Small shopkeepers, they earn their livelihood during these days. We know the hardship, difficulty and crises entire families face,” the CJI said, referring to the importance of the festive season for small businesses. “If there is loss of business, if it is unlawful to your clients, we will exercise our powers under constitutional tort jurisdiction. Let's cross that bridge when it comes,” Justice Bagchi told advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai, who mentioned the petition on behalf of a traders’ association. Dehadrai claimed that disruptions around Connaught Place were causing losses of more than ₹ 250 crore a day. He also flagged a New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) notification issued late on Thursday night ordering the closure of Central Park, arguing that the restrictions could affect traders and daily-wage earners in the area. Also Read | US singer Mary Millben, CJP's Abhijeet Dipke trade barbs over 'foreign funding' amid anti-CEC protests in Delhi Why is the CJP planning a protest? The proposed gathering at Central Park comes amid protests by the CJP and opposition parties against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had called on supporters to assemble at Central Park on Friday with the national flag, alleging that party members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka had been jailed for unfurling the Tricolour. The two were sent to five days of judicial custody for allegedly violating their peace bonds and trespassing into Jantar Mantar after Delhi Police withdrew the venue's status as a designated protest site. In its order on Thursday, the Delhi High Court had recorded an assurance from additional solicitor general Chetan Sharma that the police had already taken steps to regulate the CJP's activities and would take all possible measures under the law. The assurance followed a petition filed by Anil Kumar Gupta, a street vendor at Palika Bazar, who apprehended that the proposed gathering could lead to restrictions on roads, footpaths and Metro station entrances, directly affecting his business and the livelihoods of other vendors. news.story_lead: From insects to peacocks: Seven children's theme parks to open in Delhi over next three months A senior municipal official said that these parks are being developed under the AMRUT scheme and they contain 'sculpture play' installations. From an insect-themed park in Saket to Peacock Park in Mayur Vihar— the development work on seven theme parks for children is at an advanced stage, and these facilities will be opened to the public over a three-month period between November and January, senior municipal officials said. news.full_article_text: From insects to peacocks: Seven children's theme parks to open in Delhi over next three months A senior municipal official said that these parks are being developed under the AMRUT scheme and they contain 'sculpture play' installations. From an insect-themed park in Saket to Peacock Park in Mayur Vihar— the development work on seven theme parks for children is at an advanced stage, and these facilities will be opened to the public over a three-month period between November and January, senior municipal officials said. A senior municipal official said that these parks are being developed under the AMRUT scheme and they contain 'sculpture play' installations whereby children will be able to interact and play with the installations with different themes. A part of Ajmal Khan Park in Karol Bagh is being developed around an octopus theme; M Block Park in Greater Kailash-II will feature a ‘Garuda' theme. Parks near PVR Saket feature an insect theme, Swasthya Vihar Park near the Laxmi Nagar District Centre has a marine theme, and a park in Mayur Vihar Phase-III will highlight the peacock theme. "The installations in the insect and Aeroplane theme park areas are almost ready, and they will be opened first. By January, all seven parks will be operational," the official added. A senior MCD official said that interactive play equipment in the form of sculptures was first used at Dino Park-- developed as an extension of the Waste to Wonder Park. "In these new children's theme parks, we are setting up interactive play stations which are based on a theme. Swings, slides, balance beams, spiral tunnels and other equipment are designed on that theme. They are aimed at increasing children's curiosity, with sculptures of varying heights and shapes being created and woven into the parks in the form of functional elements, such as swings, slides, seating areas, dustbins and other accessories. The sculptures have been made using reinforced plastic and glass-reinforced cement fibre," the official explained. The insect park, for instance, features installations themed around various insects such as a Spider Rope Climber with play modifications around the legs of a giant arachnid. Other installations include ant-shaped slides, Caterpillar balance beams, and Beehive spiral tunnels, among many. "Just like innovative alterations have been made to the giant dinosaur replicas in the dinosaur park at Sarai Kale Khan, these structures will have swings, slides, climbing nets, tunnels and wall-holla weaved into the central insect replicas. ," the official added. news.full_article_text: Will award compensation if Delhi protests impact traders, daily-wagers: Supreme Court The Supreme Court expressed concern over the hardship faced by small businesses during the festive season The Supreme Court on Friday warned it would invoke its constitutional tort jurisdiction to award compensation if protests in Delhi disproportionately impede traders and daily-wage earners from pursuing their livelihoods, as it expressed concern over the hardship faced by small businesses during the festive season. Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi made the remarks after a plea raised concerns over the proposed gathering at Central Park in Connaught Place by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), while hoping that “better sense will prevail” and that the competing interests of protesters, traders and the authorities would be balanced. “If there is loss of business, if it is unlawful to your clients, we will exercise our powers under constitutional tort jurisdiction. Let’s cross that bridge when it comes,” Justice Bagchi told advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai, who mentioned the petition on behalf of a traders’ association. Deep Dive The court’s observations came a day after the Delhi High Court recorded an assurance from Delhi Police that it would take “all possible measures under the law” to regulate the proposed gathering and address apprehensions that it could disrupt business and movement in the Connaught Place area. Dehadrai told the Supreme Court that the proposed protest threatened substantial losses to traders, particularly when businesses depend on the festive season for a significant share of their earnings. He claimed that the disruption around Connaught Place was causing losses of more than ₹ 250 crore a day. “This is also related to protest. It can wait till October 26,” CJI Kant said initially, indicating that the matter would not be taken up immediately. Justice Bagchi pointed out that the Delhi High Court had heard a similar petition on Thursday. When counsel insisted that the plea before the Supreme Court raised distinct concerns, Justice Bagchi said the competing claims of protesters, traders and law enforcement agencies had to be considered together. “Someone wants to protest, someone wants to sell moongfali (peanuts), someone wants to maintain law and order. All are there before us. We can hear it after a week,” he said. The CJI hoped that the situation would be handled with due regard for the economic vulnerability of small traders and their families. “We hope better sense will prevail on everyone. Small shopkeepers...they earn their livelihood during these days. We know the hardship, difficulty and crises entire families face,” he said. Dehadrai flagged a notification issued by the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) late on Thursday night shutting Central Park, arguing that the restriction would effectively prevent traders from conducting business in the surrounding area. He referred to the impact on labourers and daily-wage earners, questioning whether the restrictions were proportionate. Justice Bagchi said the court had the power to grant relief if it ultimately found that the restrictions imposed on business and livelihood were disproportionate. “If we hold that it’s disproportionate, this court has ample jurisdiction under public and compensation law,” said the judge, indicating that the court could examine the question of compensation if the circumstances warranted it. The CJI directed that the matter be listed on October 26 or 27, after the Supreme Court’s Dussehra vacation, which runs through next week. The proposed gathering at Central Park comes amid protests by the CJP and opposition parties against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke had called on supporters to assemble at Central Park on Friday with the national flag, alleging that party members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka had been jailed for unfurling the Tricolour. The two were sent to five days of judicial custody for allegedly violating their peace bonds and trespassing into Jantar Mantar after the Delhi Police de-notified the venue as a designated protest site. In its order on Thursday, the Delhi High Court recorded an assurance from additional solicitor general Chetan Sharma that the police had already taken steps to regulate the activities of the CJP and would take all possible measures under the law. The assurance followed a petition by Anil Kumar Gupta, a street vendor at Palika Bazar, who apprehended that the proposed gathering could lead to restrictions on roads, footpaths and Metro station entrances, directly affecting his business and the livelihoods of other vendors. The police withdrew Jantar Mantar’s status as a designated protest venue and notified three alternatives -- Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground in north Delhi and CBD Ground in east Delhi. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Utkarsh Anand Utkarsh Anand is the National Legal Editor at Hindustan Times, where he leads the newspaper's coverage of the Supreme Court, constitutional law, the judiciary and the Union law ministry. He joined Hindustan Times in 2020 after stints at Press Trust of India (PTI), The Indian Express and CNN-News18, and has over two decades of experience reporting on law, governance and public policy. news.headline: Thousands march to Indian Supreme Court to demand election chief resign
news.story_lead: India's opposition party members march to the Supreme Court in protest against a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in Delhi - Published 12 October 2026 Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend.
news.full_article_text: India's opposition party members march to the Supreme Court in protest against a controversial revision of voter lists that has sparked days of unrest, in Delhi - Published 12 October 2026 Thousands of opposition supporters marched through Delhi to India's Supreme Court to demand the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud. Monday's "March for Democracy" was the latest in a series of demonstrations, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital. Thousands of protesters were detained over the weekend. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi submitted a petition to the court challenging the process, in which tens of millions of names have been struck off the voter rolls. Opposition parties allege the revision benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The Election Commission and the BJP reject the charge. For weeks requests to protest had been denied by police, citing law and order reasons. Attempts to hold a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) pressure group over the weekend led to thousands of demonstrators being detained in Delhi. Gandhi called "all opposition parties, civil society groups [and] all those who believe in democracy" to join Monday's march. In a press conference, he shared a letter that he and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge had written to Chief Justice Surya Kant, laying out their concerns with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's alleged conduct. After they filed their petition later in the day, Kant responded by saying the matter was already before the court and therefore sub judice - meaning he could not speak about it. But he added: "You have my assurance that any such petition shall be heard at the earliest possible opportunity, in accordance with the law." There was a heavy security deployment in central Delhi and along the route of the march, with restrictions on traffic and on entry and exit at some metro stations. A bus carrying Gandhi and other opposition leaders made its way to the court from Barakamba road. Supporters waved flags and chanted his name as the Congress MP and others waved through the windows. Seated a few rows behind him was Neha Bora, a student leader who has gained prominence in the protests. A few kilometres on, in a place called Mandi House, the bus stopped and Rahul Gandhi and a few others climbed on top of the vehicle to wave at supporters lining up the street in the thousands. Many protesters climbed on to other buses parked here, while some waved flags and chanted anti-government slogans to the sound of drums and lots of cheering. "If they take away our right to vote, what is left with us?" one protester asked an AFP news agency reporter. Another protester called the march "a fight to save the very fabric" of India, the world's largest democracy. Main opposition leader Rahul Gandhi holds up a copy of India's Constitution at a press conference on Monday Protesters have been demanding the country's the election chief resign over alleged electoral roll fraud Over the past week, top opposition leaders, including Gandhi, have been briefly detained several times while leading protests in central Delhi. On Sunday, the CJP - which is not a registered political party - said it would continue protesting until Kumar stepped down. The CJP, which successfully led a protest over the summer that culminated in India's federal education minister's resignation, had called for a march on Saturday to Jantar Mantar - the best-known protest site in Delhi where the last set of sit-in demonstrations had also happened. But authorities in Delhi imposed overarching restrictions that made it almost impossible for protesters to travel and reach Jantar Mantar - trains were cancelled, dozens of metro stations were shut and tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were on the roads to detain protesters. The Home Ministry has now announced demonstrations will no longer be permitted at Jantar Mantar. Three other sites have been listed as alternatives should permission be granted. Monday's demonstrations come after thousands were detained over the weekend The CJP leaders - founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka - were dramatically detained from a plane as they landed in Delhi to join the weekend protest. They were only released a day later - while Dipke returned home to attend his grandmother's funeral, Das and Ranka held a press conference where they said the protests would continue. Both leaders have said they will seek a new protest date from the police. Over the weekend, the police detained and released thousands of people, including several journalists. Some videos and photos from the protest show police dragging people, including women, by force and pushing them into buses. The BBC also captured footage , external of a policeman slapping a detained protester inside a bus. The Delhi police did not respond to questions about the use of violence against protesters. In a statement, Reporters Without Borders condemned the detention of at least 16 Indian journalists. "Covering events of public interest is not a crime. It is their job. The police's actions against the press are unacceptable," it said. Rahul Gandhi said that young Indians who had come to peacefully protest with "love in their hearts, not hatred or anger" had been beaten up. BJP President Nitin Nabin accused opposition parties and the CJP of trying to destabilise India "at the behest of foreign forces" without elaborating on who the forces were. Related topics

news.full_article_text: Karnataka Cabinet rejects mercy pleas of fiancé, her partner in 2003 Bengaluru techie murder case Karnataka Cabinet rejected mercy petitions filed by Shubha Shankaranarayana, D Arun Verma, who are serving life sentences for the December 2003 murder of 27-year-old fiancé The Karnataka Cabinet on Thursday rejected mercy petitions filed by Shubha Shankaranarayana and D Arun Verma, who are serving life sentences for the December 2003 murder of Shubha’s 27-year-old fiancé, software engineer B V Girish, in Bengaluru. The Cabinet held that the killing was premeditated and exceptionally brutal, and that the requests for clemency could not be accepted within the applicable legal framework. “The recommendation will now be sent to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot for a final decision on the petitions. The Home Department had obtained opinions from the police and prison departments before placing the matter before the Cabinet,” home minister Priyank Kharge said after the meeting on Thursday. The petitions followed a July 14, 2025, Supreme Court judgment that upheld the life sentences imposed on all four people convicted in the case. Dismissing their appeals, the court gave the convicts eight weeks to approach the governor under Article 161 of the Constitution, which empowers governors to grant pardons, suspend sentences, remit punishments or commute them in cases within the state’s executive jurisdiction. The Cabinet’s rejection does not constitute the governor’s final decision. The constitutional process will conclude when the governor decides the petitions. Girish, a software engineer at Intel in Bengaluru, and Shubha, then a fifth-semester student of an integrated BA LLB course at BMS Law College, had got engaged on December 1, 2003, and their wedding was scheduled for April 11, 2004. According to the prosecution case examined by the Supreme Court, Shubha was unwilling to marry Girish and wanted to pursue her relationship with Arun Verma, a fellow law student. Verma, then 19, was studying in the first semester of the same course. On the evening of December 3, 2003, Shubha asked Girish to take her out for dinner. He picked her up from her home at around 6.30 pm on his scooter, and they went to TGI Friday’s, a restaurant near his workplace. After dinner, the couple stopped at the Air View Point on Airport Ring Road to watch aircraft land. Between 9.30 pm and 9.40 pm, they informed their families that they had finished dinner and were returning home. At the viewing point, an assailant struck Girish on the head with a steel rod and fled. Shubha, with the help of passers-by, stopped a car and took Girish to Manipal Hospital on Airport Road. He was declared dead at 8.05 am on December 4. The prosecution alleged that the attack was part of a conspiracy to kill Girish because Shubha did not want to proceed with the marriage. Investigators subsequently arrested Shubha, Verma and two other men, A Venkatesh and Dinesh, also known as Dinakaran. The Supreme Court’s 132-page judgment examined communications between the accused in the days leading up to the murder. Phone records showed frequent exchanges between Shubha and Verma before the killing, including communications on the day of her engagement to Girish. The four accused had exchanged 56 communications on December 2, according to the judgment. On the evening of December 3, Shubha and Verma exchanged 38 text messages between 6.37 pm and 9.39 pm while she was out with Girish. The court considered the volume and timing of these communications alongside evidence about the accused persons’ relationships, the recovery of the weapon and their conduct after the attack. It found that the prosecution had established the motive and the conspiracy. The court also examined evidence that messages had been deleted from the accused persons’ phones. The communications, together with the other circumstances proved during the trial, formed part of the chain of evidence on which the convictions rested. The trial court convicted all four accused in July 2010 and sentenced them to life imprisonment. The Karnataka high court upheld the sentences later that year. The Supreme Court subsequently examined their appeals and, on July 14, 2025, confirmed the convictions and life sentences. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Arun Dev Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.

Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told the BBC that the prime minister and other ministers were unhurt when five ballistic missiles hit al-Maashiq Palace, but that many others were injured. The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said they struck "the Saudi enemy's military operations headquarters in Aden". A coalition led by Saudi Arabia backs the government and is providing air support for an offensive by pro-government forces against the Iran-backed Houthis. Yemeni Prime Minister Shaya Zindani condemned the Houthis' attack on Aden, calling it "cowardly" and a "continuation of their criminal behaviour". He said the government continued to carry out its duties and vowed that it would not weaken the resolve of its forces to continue operations against the Houthis on Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and other front lines. Earlier, the Houthis denied that they had attacked Saudi Arabia on Thursday, after the coalition said its forces had intercepted a cruise missile in the Medina region, home to one of Islam's holiest shrines. The Houthis have been launching missiles and drones at airports, oil and gas facilities, and military bases in Saudi Arabia in retaliation for the strikes on the territory that they control in western Yemen, including the capital Sanaa. On Saturday, a Houthi missile strike killed 13 people at Riyadh's international airport, which was the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade. Saudi Arabia's deputy foreign minister accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis to escalate their conflict with the kingdom. "Iran continues to arm, train and support the Houthi militia in violation of UN Security Council resolutions," Rayed Krimly told reporters, according to AFP news agency. "We think that the escalation by the Houthis at this latest stage of the conflict is encouraged by Iran," he added. There was no immediate response from Iran's government. However, it has previously denied supplying weapons to the Houthis and said it only supports them politically. Iran's foreign minister has also said it is ready to provide "any assistance necessary to facilitate the start of talks" between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the internationally-recognised government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule. A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. The conflict escalated in September after the Houthis seized part of Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint for global shipping. Their advance contributed to a rise in oil prices following six months of war between the US, Israel and Iran. Last week, pro-government forces said they had regained control of territory overlooking Bab al-Mandab after launching a major counter-offensive with the support of Saudi air strikes. At least 1,282 people have been killed and 5,890 injured in the fighting in Yemen since 6 August, according to the government's health ministry. The UN says another 201,000 people have been displaced and that there has been an alarming surge in suspected cholera cases.
